interactionPlan.concept: A Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) processes data through an alternating sequence of feature-mixing linear operations and element-wise non-linear activations.
learningObjectives: The student will map the algebraic equations of an MLP to its graphical network representation.
The student will distinguish between linear weight operations (which mix features) and non-linear activations (which act independently on single features).
The student will understand the sequential, layer-by-layer flow of data from input to output.
interactionPlan.keyInsight: The network diagram visually separates feature-mixing linear operations (crossing arrows) from element-wise non-linear activations (straight horizontal arrows).

interactions.label: Forward Pass Step
interactions.effect: Highlights specific nodes, connecting edges, and corresponding math notations (like W1, W2) while dimming the rest of the diagram.
interactions.teaches: The step-by-step sequence of operations that transform input data into an output prediction.

demo_steps.title: The Network Structure
demo_steps.narration: Look at the overall layout of this Multilayer Perceptron. The white nodes on the left are your raw inputs (x), and the white nodes on the right are your final predictions (y). The gray nodes in the middle are the hidden 'representations' the network builds along the way.
demo_steps.focus: The distinction between white input/output nodes and gray hidden nodes.

demo_steps.title: Linear Feature Mixing
demo_steps.narration: The first step is a linear transformation. Notice how the arrows from x cross over to reach the pre-activation nodes (z). The weight matrix W1 mixes the signals from all input nodes to compute these new values.
demo_steps.focus: The crossing arrows between x and the first set of z nodes, representing the matrix multiplication W1.

demo_steps.title: Element-wise Activation
demo_steps.narration: Next, a non-linear activation function (like ReLU) is applied to get the hidden node values (h). Notice that the arrows here are straight and don't cross! This operation acts independently on each node.
demo_steps.focus: The straight horizontal arrows connecting z nodes to their corresponding h nodes.

demo_steps.title: Repeating the Pattern
demo_steps.narration: This structural pattern repeats to form a deep network. The hidden features (h) are mixed again by weight matrix W2 into a new set of pre-activations, followed by another independent ReLU activation.
demo_steps.focus: The alternating pattern of crossing arrows (W2) and straight arrows in the middle of the network.

demo_steps.title: Producing the Output
demo_steps.narration: Finally, the last weight matrix W3 maps the highest-level hidden features to your output classes (y). By chaining these linear and non-linear transformations, the network can model highly complex data distributions.
demo_steps.focus: The final set of crossing arrows (W3) pointing to the white output nodes y.

interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: A horizontal feed-forward neural network diagram. Consists of 4 pairs of nodes plus output nodes, arranged left-to-right. Leftmost: two white nodes (x1, x2). Next: two gray nodes (z11, z12) connected to x by crossing arrows. Next: two gray nodes (h11, h12) connected to z by straight horizontal arrows. Pattern repeats for z21/z22 and h21/h22. Rightmost: two white output nodes (y1, y2). Underneath the crossing arrow sections, place labels W1, W2, W3 with vertical ellipses indicating matrices. Node labels should be subscripted (e.g., z_{12} where 1 is layer, 2 is index).
